I read the whole file. I also grepped for `isTotallyReal_of_sq_ratCast_of_nonneg` across the repository. It is called in three places: this file at lines 85 and 275, and the Quadratic/InfinitePlace.lean file at line 48. It is defined in NumberField/InfinitePlace/Basic.lean at line 122.

The only repeated reasoning I found is the "adjoining a square root of a nonnegative rational gives a totally real field" step. In `isTotallyReal_candidateGenusFieldBase` it is proved for `candidateGenusFieldBase hd`. In `exists_algHom_candidateGenusFieldReal` it is proved for `adjoin ℚ {z}`. Both calls reduce to the existing lemma plus a short `norm_num` check that the square equals `d`, and a generation fact that differs between the two uses. Factoring that out would be a thin wrapper around existing API, and it would save only a few lines. That is below the rubric's bar.

The other long proofs, `finrank_adjoin_candidateGenusFieldRealBaseRoot` and `isUnramifiedIn_candidateGenusFieldReal`, each appear once. The two copies of the quadratic base are handled by a single equivalence. I did not run Lean, so a replacement I did not test could still fail.
